memory_candidates: Under the current Lean toolchain, `cases x` (and `rcases ... with rfl`) CLEARS the scrutinee variable; recognizer arms that previously kept the variable accessible must use named constructor binders and reference the constructor form (.atom n / .imp a b / .box a) instead of the cleared variable.

A `def f (b) (acc) : Prop := exists (W : Type*) ...` over a section `variable {Atom : Type*}` has TWO universe params [Atom-univ, witness-univ]; `f.{u}` pins the FIRST (Atom) slot, which is usually wrong. To share the existential witness universe between a hypothesis and the goal, declare `universe v; variable {Atom : Type v}` and pin both slots with `f.{v, v}`.

An incorrect universe pin can produce a FALSE-GREEN build: when the goal type fails to elaborate, Lean error-recovers and the entire proof body type-checks against a recovered (sorry-like) goal, hiding the real per-leaf errors until the universe is corrected.

Current Lean `split_ifs at h` auto-discharges branches whose hypothesis becomes `none = some _`, leaving only the satisfiable branch; nested per-condition `split_ifs` then fails with 'no if-then-else'. Use a single `split_ifs ... with a b` and drop the absurd bullets.
